cards.title: What is equality?
cards.text: Equality means everyone gets the same respect and fair chances, whatever their gender, caste, religion or background.

cards.title: Gender equality
cards.text: Women and men should have equal rights, pay and opportunities. When women progress, families and nations do too.

cards.title: Women’s empowerment
cards.text: Empowerment means giving women education, safety and the power to make their own choices.

cards.title: Why educate girls
cards.text: An educated girl earns more, marries later, raises healthier children and lifts her community.

cards.title: Stereotypes
cards.text: A stereotype is a fixed idea about a group, like “girls can’t play sports”. It limits potential.

options: A fixed, unfair idea about a group

cards.title: Human rights
cards.text: Human rights belong to everyone just for being human, like life, freedom, education and fair treatment.

cards.title: Discrimination
cards.text: Discrimination is treating people unfairly because of who they are. It harms dignity and opportunity.

cards.title: Caste and equality
cards.text: The Constitution bans discrimination by caste and religion. Real change also needs attitudes to change.

qs.q: Beyond laws, ending caste bias needs…

cards.title: Safety for women
cards.text: Safe streets, quick justice, good lighting and respectful education all help women feel secure.

qs.q: A step towards women’s safety is…

cards.title: Equal pay
cards.text: Equal pay for equal work is fair. Pay gaps hurt women’s independence.

cards.title: Inclusion
cards.text: Inclusion means making room for everyone, including persons with disabilities, and removing barriers.

options: Everyone belongs and can take part

cards.title: Respect for differences
cards.text: Societies thrive when people respect differences in language, faith and ways of life.

cards.title: Child rights
cards.text: Every child has the right to learn, be safe, be healthy and be heard.

cards.title: Child labour
cards.text: Children working instead of studying lose their future and health. Poverty is a major cause.

qs.q: A main cause of child labour is…

cards.title: Right to education
cards.text: Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 is a fundamental right in India.

cards.title: Why children drop out
cards.text: Poverty, distance, child marriage and poor teaching make some children leave school.

qs.q: A reason children drop out is…

cards.title: Mid-day meals
cards.text: Free school meals bring poor children to school and improve nutrition.

cards.title: Bullying
cards.text: Bullying hurts self-esteem and learning. Schools should make it safe to speak up.

cards.title: Child marriage
cards.text: Marrying children too early ends their education and harms health. It is illegal in India.

cards.title: Homelessness
cards.text: Many families lack proper housing. Shelters, jobs and affordable homes help.

cards.title: Street children
cards.text: Street children need care, schooling and safety. NGOs and communities can help.

cards.title: Social responsibility
cards.text: Everyone should contribute to society by volunteering, being kind and helping those in need.

cards.title: Role of NGOs
cards.text: NGOs fill gaps by helping with education, health and disasters, working alongside government.

cards.title: Persons with disabilities
cards.text: Ramps, braille and inclusive classrooms let persons with disabilities learn and work with dignity.

cards.title: What is culture?
cards.text: Culture is a group’s shared language, food, festivals, art and values passed down through generations.

cards.title: Unity in diversity
cards.text: India has many languages, faiths and customs, yet people share one nation. This is its strength.

cards.title: Tradition and change
cards.text: Traditions give identity, but societies must change harmful customs and keep what is good.

cards.title: Values
cards.text: Honesty, kindness, courage and respect are values that guide how we treat others.

cards.title: Joint vs nuclear families
cards.text: Joint families offer support, nuclear families offer privacy. Each has pros and cons.

cards.title: Generation gap
cards.text: Young and old often differ in views. Listening and respect bridge the gap.

cards.title: Consumerism
cards.text: Buying things to look successful can harm budgets and the planet. Needs differ from wants.

cards.title: Urbanisation
cards.text: Cities offer jobs and facilities but bring crowding, pollution and pressure on housing.

qs.q: A downside of rapid urbanisation is…

cards.title: Migration
cards.text: People move for jobs, education or safety. It spreads ideas but strains cities.

cards.title: Festivals
cards.text: Festivals bring people together, preserve traditions and support local artisans.

cards.title: Tolerance
cards.text: Tolerance means accepting that others may think or live differently.

cards.title: Elders and respect
cards.text: Looking after elders repays their care and keeps wisdom alive in families.
